The provided text discusses quantum computing, specifically highlighting the use of qubits to enhance computational power for cryptography and drug discovery. This concept can be linked to existing knowledge in computer science and biology databases. In cryptography, the shift from classical bits to quantum qubits necessitates the development of post-quantum cryptography to secure data against future quantum attacks. In pharmaceuticals, the ability of quantum systems to model complex molecular structures allows for more accurate simulations of drug interactions, potentially accelerating the discovery of new treatments. These connections illustrate how advancements in quantum mechanics are directly influencing practical applications in security and healthcare.
